name: @material-tax-reporting/cra-pdf
description: Tax-year-versioned local preparation of CRA mail-in PDF packages after mandatory manual review; no electronic filing.
//: The '.' entry names TypeScript source, and there is deliberately no compiled
'node' condition and no build script, because nothing consumes this package yet.
Outside prose — this package's README, and the repository's documentation and
changelog records — the specifier appears only as this manifest's own name, and no
manifest, bundler alias, build script, test or workflow resolves it. A build step
nothing runs is a build step nobody maintains.
It replaces an entry that could not have worked. 'main', 'types' and both export
conditions named files under ./dist, which is git-ignored and which nothing in this
repository produces: the 'build' script meant to produce them ran 'tsc', and
TypeScript is declared in no manifest here, appears in neither lockfile, and is
installed nowhere, so that script had never run once. Every consumer, bundler and
Node alike, would have failed with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND naming a compiled file no
command in this repository can create.
The relative specifiers inside src/ moved with the entry, from '.js' to '.ts',
matching packages/surface-kernel. They were written in the NodeNext convention,
where './adapter.js' exists only after a TypeScript emit — an emit nothing here
performs — and stripping types does not rewrite a specifier, so that source could
not be loaded by Node at any version, including one new enough to strip types. With
'.ts' specifiers a bundler and a type-stripping Node both read it: esbuild resolves
this package by name through this entry and bundles it, and Node 26.4.0 imports it
by name and loads all 28 exports.
THE TRAP, if you are the first to import this from a file Node executes directly:
the pinned toolchain cannot load a '.ts' file at all. Type stripping arrived in Node
22.18.0, which is newer than the 22.13.0 and 22.14.0 the workflows pin, so you will
get ERR_UNKNOWN_FILE_EXTENSION naming src/index.ts. Fix it by copying
packages/surface-kernel rather than improvising: add a 'node' condition ahead of
'default' naming ./dist/index.js; add scripts/build.mjs that transpiles with esbuild
and never with tsc, which type-checks and so could withhold a release on a verdict;
add 'esbuild' both to this manifest and to this package's node in package-lock.json
in that same commit, because the release path installs with 'npm ci' and that
refuses a manifest and a lockfile which disagree; and add a 'prebuild' hook in the
consuming workspace exactly as apps/desktop already does for surface-kernel, so the
ordering is inherited rather than repeated at every call site.
Until then this manifest declares no dependency and no 'engines' field, which is why
package-lock.json's record of this package is still accurate and needs no
regeneration.
